summary.text: A male infant born at 40 weeks (3.6 kg) after normal routine prenatal ultrasounds was discharged as healthy, received an oral rotavirus vaccine on postnatal day 57, developed lethargy, decreased milk intake and increased defecation frequency from day 58, and presented at 2 months with sudden lethargy, pallor and cyanosis.

On arrival at the emergency department he had severe respiratory distress and circulatory collapse, with central cyanosis and poor perfusion before cardiac arrest; despite resuscitation he died of acute heart failure within two hours of presentation.

Forensic autopsy showed cardiomegaly with marked right ventricular hypertrophy and an atrial septal defect, with myocardial hypertrophy, contraction band necrosis and interstitial fibrosis on histology; the final pathological diagnosis was congenital heart disease (HCM and ASD) leading to death from acute heart failure.

Trio whole-exome sequencing identified compound heterozygous MYBPC3 variants, a paternal splice-site variant c.2905+1G>A and a novel maternal frameshift deletion c.836del (p.Gly279Valfs*21); the text calls both pathogenic whereas Table 3 classifies c.836del as likely pathogenic. Both parents are heterozygous carriers who have cardiac surveillance (mild mitral regurgitation) and initiated IVF with preimplantation genetic testing.

Autopsy findings and histological analysis of the cardiac abnormalities. (a) Heart morphology demonstrating overall enlargement, particularly of the right atrium and right ventricle (HP:0001667). (l,m) Sanger sequencing validation of MYBPC3variants in the proband and parents. with one variant inherited from the father and the other from the mother.
